title: Augmented strict-poset chains with alternating deletion
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $P$ a partially ordered set. For $n\in\mathbf Z$ let $B_n(P)$ consist of lists $l$ of elements of $P$ satisfying $l_a<l_b$ whenever $a<b$ and $|l|=n+1$. Define $C_n(P;R)=\{a:B_n(P)\to R\mid a\text{ has finite support}\}$, with pointwise module operations. For any list $l$, write $[l]_n$ for its unit basis vector if $l\in B_n(P)$, and zero otherwise; in particular repeated weakly increasing lists denote zero. Thus $B_{-1}(P)$ has the unique empty list, $C_{-1}(P;R)$ is canonically $R$ on $[\varnothing]$, and $C_n(P;R)=0$ for $n<-1$. Define $d_{ij}$ to be zero unless $i=j+1$, and in that case extend the rule $d_{ij}[l]_i=\sum_{a=0}^{|l|-1}(-1)^a[l\text{ with vertex }a\text{ deleted}]_j$ linearly. Let $C(P;R)$ be the integer-indexed chain complex [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology] with these terms and differentials; the chain-complex proof obligation is the cancellation of each double deletion in the two possible orders. In particular a vertex maps to the empty generator and the empty generator has zero differential.

source.place: Tag 019S, lemma-homotopy-s-N and preceding equation-homotopy-to-homotopy (lines 4739–4846); the explicit augmented strict-poset adaptation and double-deletion construction in lem-sfb-poset-augmented-chain-prism, statement and proof steps 1–2.

proof.text: For any function f from lists to an R-module, let D(f)(l) be the alternating sum of f(l.eraseIdx a). Splitting off index zero shows D(f)(x :: l) = f(l) - D(t ↦ f(x :: t))(l). The same finite sum preserves subtraction.

Induct on l, generalizing f, to prove D(D(f))(l) = 0. The empty list gives the empty sum. For x :: l, the preceding recurrence and additivity give D(f)(l) - (D(f)(l) - D(D(t ↦ f(x :: t)))(l)); the induction hypothesis and additive cancellation finish.

The off-shape boundary is zero by definition. For adjacent degrees evaluate each boundary on a strict-chain basis generator using linearCombination_single. Every deletion remains pairwise strict, and its length decreases by one. Thus the composite on a generator is D(D(bracket))(l), which vanishes by the list induction. Linear-map and Finsupp extensionality finish. The empty-list case includes the augmentation and all negative degrees.
